llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Accredible Certificates connector wrapper with expected read, create, and delete capabilities plus user-confirmation safeguards for state-changing actions.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to operate Accredible Certificates through an OOMOL-connected account, and the documented actions are limited to credential and group read/search/list plus credential create/delete operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger wording is broad for any Accredible Certificates request, but it stays within the named service and the runtime instructions explicitly require schema inspection and user confirmation for write or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself contains only a SKILL.md file and allows Bash(oo *) commands; first-time setup includes remote oo CLI install commands, disclosed as fallback steps only when the CLI is missing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The requested tool access is scoped to the oo CLI, credentials are described as injected server-side by OOMOL, and no local credential scraping or broad filesystem indexing is present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background workers, privilege escalation, or hidden persistence are present; account sign-in and service connection are expected one-time setup for this connector.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let your agent use your OOMOL-connected Accredible account. Review create and delete payloads carefully before approval, and only run the oo CLI installation step if you trust OOMOL's installer source.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad invocation wording is real, but artifact review shows a single-service connector with clear action labels and explicit confirmation requirements for write and destructive actions, so it does not justify Review by itself.
[static-scan] expected: Static scan reported no suspicious patterns, consistent with the artifact containing only declarative skill instructions.
[virustotal-engines] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean across supplied engines and provides no negative signal.
